posts.name: Cindy Garcia
posts.cooked:
Hi, I’m Cindy. I build n8n and Make automations full time, and fixed price is how I prefer to work anyway, so this fits.

Three things I’ve built recently:

A real estate valuation form for a broker in Ohio. Webhook off his website form, address geocoded through Google Maps, then into his MLS API to pull comps and send a valuation back to the site. Most of the real work was in the failure points, addresses that don’t match anything, searches that come back empty, the webhook never actually responding to the form.

A cold outreach system that pulls leads, verifies every email address, writes a personalized opening line for each one off that business’s own website, loads them into the sending platform, then watches the replies and sorts them.

A content pipeline that takes a script, generates the video through an API, and schedules it out to six platforms on a set cadence, with checks in the middle that stop a bad one from going out.

On price. A small project, something like a form to CRM connection or a handful of API calls with real error handling, I’m usually at $500 fixed. A medium one, multi step with an AI piece or a messy API in the middle, runs $1,200 to $1,800 depending on how many unknowns there are.

I can start this week. I’m in California, Pacific time.

The one thing I’d want to understand better before a first project is the payment side. Paid after your client approves the milestone makes sense from where you sit. I’d just want to know how long that usually takes in practice, and what you’d do if a client goes quiet after the work is delivered and working.

Happy to look at whatever you have in front of you right now if you want to send it over.
